skill.name: slideshow
skill.description: Guides AI agents to create HyperFrames slideshow compositions with slides, fragments, branch navigation, presenter notes, media handling, and validation.
skill.summary: Create interactive HyperFrames slide decks with presenter mode and validation.
skill.author: heygen-com

One low-severity issue remains: the optional Three.js reference imports code from a CDN if copied into a deck. No prompt-injection attempt, secret handling, or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Optional Three.js reference loads a CDN module at runtime.
remediation.suggestion: Use a local bundled Three.js dependency or clearly require generated projects to download and commit the dependency before handoff.

content.value_statement: Teams need structured slide decks that preserve motion, media, and interaction. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to author HyperFrames slideshow compositions.
actual_capabilities: Defines slideshow manifests with slides, slide sequences, fragments, hotspots, notes, and reserved TTS fields.
Explains how scenes connect to slide references through composition IDs and timing attributes.
Provides rules for pitch decks, source-page conversions, media handling, and readable slide layouts.
Documents presenter mode, audience sync, editable notes, global mute, and media cleanup behavior.
Includes standalone wrapper patterns for browser demos before engine-hosted preview support is available.
Lists lint and runtime validation commands for completed slideshow projects.
limitations: TTS fields are reserved, but playback is not wired in the documented slideshow flow.
Standalone wrapper guidance is temporary and may change when engine-hosted slideshow preview ships.
The skill assumes access to HyperFrames player bundles, CLI commands, and project files.
Browser autoplay and audience media sync still require runtime validation in a real browser.

use_cases.title: Create an interactive pitch deck
use_cases.description: Turn a product story into claim-led slides with fragments, speaker notes, and branchable detail sections.

use_cases.title: Convert a web page into a deck
use_cases.description: Preserve source visuals, media behavior, and motion while changing page movement into slide navigation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a presenter-ready demo
use_cases.description: Build a runnable HyperFrames entrypoint with navigation, presenter mode, media cleanup, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic slideshow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HyperFrames slideshow for this topic. Use clear slide claims, speaker notes, and simple navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a page into slides
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this existing page into a HyperFrames slideshow. Preserve the visual design, media behavior, and key interactions.

prompt_templates.title: Add reveals and branches
prompt_templates.prompt: Add fragment reveals and hotspot branches to this deck. Keep the main path concise and put extra detail in branches.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare presenter handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Make this slideshow presenter-ready. Add the runnable entrypoint, verify media cleanup, and list the validation results.

output_examples.input: A founder asks for a seed pitch deck with a market-sizing branch.
output_examples.output: A runnable deck plan with claim-led slides, speaker notes, a market detail branch, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A designer provides a landing page and asks for a presentation version.
output_examples.output: A slide sequence that keeps the page style, translates scroll motion into navigation, and preserves media controls.

output_examples.input: An engineer needs a browser-openable demo for a customer review.
output_examples.output: A presenter-ready slideshow entrypoint with shared navigation, media mute behavior, and a concise handoff note.

best_practices: Confirm the user wants a HyperFrames slideshow before authoring adjacent presentation requests.
Keep one idea and one visual on each slide, with readable text and clear claims.
Run lint and runtime validation before handoff, then fix all reported slideshow contract issues.
anti_patterns: Do not hide the slideshow manifest behind runtime code or alternate script types.
Do not add custom presenter, mute, or note-editing controls when shared player behavior exists.
Do not crop screenshots, product UI, charts, or documents when they contain meaningful information.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates HyperFrames slideshow compositions with discrete slides, navigation, fragments, branches, and presenter support.

faq.question: Does it replace normal HyperFrames composition rules?
faq.answer: No. It extends the base composition contract with slideshow-specific manifest and navigation rules.

faq.question: Can it convert an existing web page?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides conversion while preserving source visuals, motion, interactions, and media behavior where practical.

faq.question: Does it support presenter notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents shared editable presenter notes that layer local changes over manifest notes.

faq.question: Are text-to-speech fields active?
faq.answer: No. TTS fields are reserved in the schema, but playback is not wired in this flow.

faq.question: How should completed decks be checked?
faq.answer: Run the HyperFrames lint and validation commands, then treat reported contract messages as blockers.
